noticeTitle: Belgium – Training services – Framework Contract for Training Activities and Knowledge Management in the fields of Civil Protection and Disaster Risk Management
procedureTitle: Framework Contract for Training Activities and Knowledge Management in the fields of Civil Protection and Disaster Risk Management
description: The general objective of the Framework Contract is to assist the Commission in the implementation of the Disaster Resilience Goals; key actions of the Preparedness Union Strategy in the fields of competence of DG ECHO; key initiatives of the Knowledge Network; and the UCPM Training and Exercises Programme by addressing more rapidly any identified knowledge and skills gaps in the UCPM. The specific objectives of the Framework Contract are to facilitate evidence-based policy making with reliable knowledge, evidence, analysis and policy guidance on specific subject areas related to the field of the disaster risk management, civil protection and crisis management which could have multi-sectorial and multi-disciplinary focus; and to strengthen capacity building in the field of disaster risk management, civil protection and crisis management by enhancing knowledge, skills and exchange of good practice and lessons learned. The core of the services provided under this framework contract is the development, design and delivery of online modules, ad-hoc training courses, training of trainers, thematic seminars and workshops, summer/winter schools, seminars and studies. The current framework agreement will expire on 13 March 2026.

noticeTitle: Belgium – Research and development services and related consultancy services – European Natural Hazard Scientific Partnership (ENHSP)
procedureTitle: European Natural Hazard Scientific Partnership (ENHSP)
description: The envisaged European Natural Hazard Scientific Partnership (ENHSP) shall offer a 24/7 stand-by emergency reporting service to facilitate and improve the analysis and assessment capacities of the Emergency Response Coordination Centre (ERCC), a regular multi-hazard monitoring service, and a scientific expertise on-demand service. The services will strengthen the capacity of the ERCC in the field of anticipation, preparedness, planning, monitoring, analysis, early warning and information. In addition, the envisaged ENHSP will deliver emergency advisory service also to EU Member States and Participating States to the Union Civil Protection Mechanism (UCPM) as well as training and exercises. The envisaged ENHSP will be composed of a network of scientific and research institutes covering at least the following natural hazards and including potential cascading effects (e.g., dam break), at the global level: severe weather; earthquakes; tsunamis; floods; volcanic events and wildfires. It will form part of the ERCC's Scientific and Technical Advisory Facility (STAF) which has been established according to article 3.e and 8.c of the Decision 1313/2013, encouraging to fully exploit science in disaster risk management, further develop transnational early warning systems and build a comprehensive situational awareness through the development of European scientific partnerships. Under STAF, the European Scientific partnerships, including the envisaged ENHSP, provide with scientific advice the ERCC and the UCPM allowing better anticipation, planning, preparedness for and response to disasters.
